title: Earlier shared errors reduced shortage-fraction forecast loss by 21% at 166 NRCS sites in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested a joint-risk supplement to NRCS April 1 runoff bounds. At 166 sites in four western US drainage regions, each with a complete 2000-2025 record, we forecast the fraction below the issued lower bound. For each test year in 2013-2025, we used earlier failure years only. Resampling years together reduced continuous ranked probability score by 21.3% against independent sites, with 95% whole-year limits of 11.9-34.7%. Both methods had exactly the same site probabilities and mean failure count. Fixed earlier training gave a 23.6% gain. In an added test against independent regions that kept within-region dependence, the gain was only 2.8% (-5.3 to 7.8%). Thus the evidence supports dependence within the network, but does not establish added forward value from cross-region links. Severe failures remained unresolved: at least a quarter of sites failed in two of thirteen years, while shared years assigned 6.8% probability on average. This is an archive forecast of failure fractions, not a forecast of physical water volume or an official joint NRCS product. Revised data, complete-panel selection, nested sites and thirteen test years limit inference. Code, exact aggregate distributions, source hashes and checks are included; external records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Shared earlier failure years improve the pooled count-distribution score against independent sites. Regional bars show pointwise whole-year intervals.
